learning.learning_goal: Understand that 'how many fewer' asks for the same gap from the other direction.
learning.big_idea: Fewer compares two amounts by finding the gap.

screens.label: Lesson 002
screens.title: How many fewer?
screens.body: Fewer is another way to compare two groups.

screens.label: Misconception
screens.title: Is the smaller amount the answer?
screens.prompt: There are 16 apples and 9 oranges. How many fewer oranges are there than apples?

choices.text: 9, because oranges are the smaller group
7, because fewer asks for the gap
choices.feedback: Fewer asks how far apart the two amounts are.

hints: The question does not ask how many oranges there are.
Compare 16 and 9 by finding their gap.

visual.message: Both rows start in the same place. Which row stops sooner?

screens.label: Discover
screens.title: What does fewer ask us to find?

visual.message: The gap shows how many fewer blocks the bottom row has.

choices.feedback: Fewer asks for the gap between the two groups.

hints: The gap tells how many fewer.

screens.label: Language
screens.title: Fewer, less, difference.

visual.message: These words compare the two groups.

screens.guidance: Fewer does not mean guess smaller. It asks how far apart the groups are.

screens.label: Remember
screens.title: Fewer still means find the gap.
screens.hook: Larger amount − smaller amount = how many fewer
screens.body: The direction of the comparison changes, but the size of the gap stays the same.

screens.label: Symbol
screens.title: Which equation measures fewer?

visual.message: The gap is still measured from larger to smaller.

choices.feedback: The larger amount minus the smaller amount gives the gap.

hints: Measure the gap from larger to smaller.

visual.message: The bottom row has 6 fewer blocks.

screens.label: Guided practice
screens.title: How many fewer are in the shorter row?

visual.message: Match eight blocks in each row. The unmatched blocks show how many fewer.

choices.feedback: 14 − 8 = 6, so the shorter row has 6 fewer blocks.

hints: Count the blocks without a match.

screens.label: Independent practice
screens.title: Solve without the model.
screens.prompt: A bus has 17 adults and 12 children. How many fewer children are there than adults?
hints: The question asks for the gap, not the number of children.
Subtract the smaller amount from the larger amount.

screens.label: Recall
screens.title: What does fewer ask you to find?
screens.prompt: Choose the rule that works for a how-many-fewer comparison.

choices.text: Find the gap from larger to smaller
choices.feedback: Fewer compares the amounts by measuring their gap.

hints: Recall the memory hook: fewer still means find the gap.

screens.label: Transfer
screens.title: Use the idea in a new setting.
screens.prompt: Jamal walked 23 blocks and Priya walked 15 blocks. How many fewer blocks did Priya walk?
hints: Walking distance is a new context, but fewer still asks for the gap.

screens.label: Reflect
screens.title: What did you discover?
screens.prompt: Choose the statement that explains the idea.

choices.text: Fewer always means the smaller number is the answer.
Fewer can ask for the gap between two groups.

hints: Think about what the missing part showed.

screens.title: You compared with fewer.
screens.body: You used the same gap idea from a new direction.
